column5: C# permits an application-defined IEnvelopeHeader implementation Stranger. Rust uses a closed EnvelopeHeader enum, with no user-defined header-kind implementation and no unsafe construction; this exact extensible-interface input is native to C#.

column3: Refuses_to_write_past_the_bytes_it_is_given
column5: The source supplies a 31-byte destination span for a 32-byte header. Rust write_header takes a growable Vec and appends storage; a fixed undersized caller span is no input of this writer. Header sizing and exact writes remain fully tested.

column3: Copies_the_payload_out_of_the_bytes_it_read
column5: The source mutates a byte array after reading its Result payload and requires the old payload bytes. Rust read_envelope accepts immutable Bytes and safely shares its backing storage by slicing. Rust cannot mutate that shared backing store while the payload lives; copying/allocation identity is a platform-specific mechanism, not an input mutation possible through this Rust API. The active offset test reads a Bytes slice five bytes into its pool.

column3: Refuses_to_write_an_envelope_whose_body_is_not_its_kind_s
column5: C# Envelope independently stores its header, optional failure and payload, admitting an absent chunk payload, absent failure record, a failure beside a result, and bytes beside a cancel. Rust Envelope is a closed enum whose variants require their own body and expose no extra body slot. An empty chunk is representable and retains its separate active runtime refusal twin.
